# jellyfin_plugin (Resource)

Installs a plugin on the Jellyfin server. The server may require a restart after installation.

Jellyfin's *Update Plugins* scheduled task (key `PluginUpdates`) upgrades every plugin to the newest compatible version its repositories offer, at startup and every 24 hours by default. While that task has at least one trigger, automatic updates are on and `version` is a minimum: any installed version at least as new satisfies it, and creating the resource adopts a newer installed version instead of installing an older one. While the task has no triggers, or the server has no such task, `version` is exact, and the next apply reinstalls the configured version over any other. The setting is global; the `autoUpdate` flag in a plugin's `meta.json` is not read. Creating the resource never keeps a version Jellyfin lists as `NotSupported` or `Malfunctioned`: it installs the configured version, and fails if no enabled repository offers a build of it for this server.

To hold every plugin at its configured version, remove the task's triggers with `jellyfin_scheduled_task`. When a `jellyfin_scheduled_task` manages `PluginUpdates`, give each `jellyfin_plugin` `depends_on = [jellyfin_scheduled_task.<name>]`, so Terraform applies the schedule first, and one apply that removes the triggers also reinstalls the plugins the task moved past their `version`. Without it, a plan that turns updates on or off can fail and ask for it. Keep the task and the plugins on one provider configuration. A plan that cannot know the schedule, such as with triggers unknown until apply or `-refresh=false`, warns, and the next plan corrects it.

Replacing the resource also replaces the resources that take its `id`, such as `jellyfin_plugin_configuration`, because the `id` is unknown until the plugin is installed again. They then write their configuration again, which Jellyfin accepts only once a restart has loaded the reinstalled plugin, so put a `jellyfin_restart` between them, as the `jellyfin_security_plugin_configuration` example does.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "jellyfin_plugin" "example" {
  name           = "Bookshelf"
  version        = "13.0.0.0"
  repository_url = "https://repo.jellyfin.org/files/plugin/manifest.json"

  # The Update Plugins schedule decides whether version is a minimum or exact,
  # so apply it before the plugin.
  depends_on = [jellyfin_scheduled_task.plugin_updates]
}

# Jellyfin's Update Plugins task upgrades every plugin at startup and daily.
# While it has triggers, version is a minimum, so Bookshelf may run a newer
# release. With no triggers, as here, no plugin updates automatically and
# Bookshelf stays at exactly 13.0.0.0.
resource "jellyfin_scheduled_task" "plugin_updates" {
  key      = "PluginUpdates"
  triggers = []
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The plugin package name. Used as the import key (e.g. `terraform import jellyfin_plugin.x "SSO-Auth"`).

### Optional

- `repository_url` (String) The repository URL from which to install the plugin. Required when creating the resource and resolved automatically on import when the exact package version is still available.
- `version` (String) The version to install, as the repository lists it (e.g. `13.0.0.0`), or `latest` (the newest offered) or `supported` (the Jellyfin Security release this provider was tested against). A keyword is resolved only at install or when set, stays in state as written, and accepts any version installed later. Omitted, it installs as `supported` for Jellyfin Security and `latest` otherwise, then tracks `installed_version`, as it also does after a keyword is removed. A version is a minimum while automatic plugin updates are on, else exact; see the resource description. Changing it reinstalls the plugin, replacing the resource, unless the installed version already satisfies the new value.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The plugin ID assigned by Jellyfin after installation.
- `installed_version` (String) The version Jellyfin lists for the plugin, which can be newer than `version` while automatic plugin updates are on. While an update waits for a restart, this keeps the previous version, whose `status` reads `Superseded`. A version Jellyfin deletes at the next restart is ignored.
- `status` (String) The status Jellyfin lists for `installed_version`: `Active` (loaded), `Restart` (waiting for a restart to load), `Superseded` (a newer version waits for a restart to replace it), `Disabled` (disabled on the dashboard's Plugins page), `NotSupported` (built for another Jellyfin version, so not loaded) or `Malfunctioned` (failed to load; the server log says why). Creating the resource fails if the version it installed is `NotSupported` or `Malfunctioned`, and the next apply replaces the tainted plugin.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import jellyfin_plugin.example "<plugin-name>"
```
